content.text:
## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

content.text:
Static HTML project. I'll build a top-down racing game with canvas 2D, no dependencies. Needs to be polished: track, car physics, lap timing, best lap, AI opponents maybe, drift marks, minimap, mobile touch controls, sound.

Let me plan the game design:

"Simple top down racing game" - I'll make a single-file-ish set of files: index.html, style.css, game.js (maybe modules). Static so no build.

Design:
- Top-down view, camera follows car, world bigger than viewport.
- Track: closed circuit defined by a centerline spline (Catmull-Rom), with width ~ 190px. Render asphalt ribbon with kerbs, dashed center line? Actually racing: asphalt, white edge lines, red/white kerbs, grass background with texture, checkered start line.
- Car physics: arcade drift model with velocity vector, steering, grip, lateral friction, drift when handbrake/high speed. Car sprite drawn with canvas paths (body, windows, wheels rotate, headlights).
- AI opponents: follow racing line with lookahead, steering, speed control, collision avoid-ish. 3 AI cars.
- Laps: progress via nearest centerline index, check crossing line, 3 laps race. Timer, best lap, position (1st/4th).
- HUD: speedometer, gear?, lap counter, lap times, minimap, countdown 3-2-1-GO, results overlay, pause.
- Controls: WASD/arrows, Space handbrake, R restart. Touch: on-screen steering buttons + throttle/brake + drift. Mobile responsive.
- Audio: WebAudio engine sound (oscillator pitch by speed), tyre screech noise, countdown beeps, skip toggle.
- Visual polish: camera slight rotation? Keep top-down fixed orientation but camera follows and rotates? Top-down racing classic: fixed orientation with camera follow is simpler and readable. Could add slight rotation based on velocity direction for immersion, but minimap/readability. I'll do camera that follows and looks ahead slightly, no rotation (up = north), which is a top-down racer. Actually rotation-based chase is nice too. Let's do fixed north-up with camera follow, plus zoom out at speed slightly.

Hmm, "top down racing game" — maybe more fun with rotating camera aligned to car heading? Many top-down racers (Micro Machines) are fixed. I'll do fixed with subtle lead.

Track design: Use points forming an interesting circuit. Let's define in world coordinates roughly 2400x1600.

Track centerline points (closed):
(400,900), (300,600), (450,380), (800,300), (1150,380), (1350,550), (1300,760), (1000,820), (900,1000), (1050,1180), (1400,1200), (1650,1050), (1900,1080), (2050,850), (1950,600), (1650,480)... hmm need smooth non-self-intersecting.

Better to generate a smooth loop from parametric shape: radius modulation around an oval. e.g. center (1200, 800), rx 850, ry 520, radius scale varying with angle: r = 1 + 0.18*sin(3θ) + 0.1*cos(2θ). That gives a wavy loop, smooth and non-intersecting. Track width ~200. This is reliable and creates nice corners. Let's do that, sample 400 points, then maybe smooth.

World bounds then about 300..2100 x 200..1400. Camera zoom ~0.82.

Width: 200 world px — car ~46px long, so track width ~4 car widths. Good.

Start/finish at angle 0 point (right side) with heading tangent. Grid start positions behind start line along track with lateral offsets.

Car physics (arcade):
- state: pos, angle (heading), vel (vector), angularVel maybe. Simple model:
  - throttle -> engine force along heading, brake -> opposite.
  - steering angle depends on speed (reduce at high speed).
  - lateral velocity damped by grip (higher grip = less sliding); handbrake reduces grip and adds yaw.
  Use "bicycle-ish" discrete model commonly used:

```
const forward = {cos, sin}
let vLong = dot(vel, forward)
let vLat = dot(vel, right)
// engine
vLong += throttle*accel*dt - drag*vLong*dt - brake...
// steering -> yaw rate
const speedFactor = clamp(abs(vLong)/maxSpeed,0,1)
const steer = steerInput * maxSteer * (1 - 0.55*speedFactor)
// yaw rate proportional to vLong * tan(steer)/wheelbase
const yawRate = vLong/wheelbase * tan(steer)
angle += yawRate*dt
// lateral grip: kill lateral velocity (friction)
vLat *= exp(-grip*dt)  with grip lower when handbrake
// recompose vel from new heading
```
This yields drifting. Add tire smoke when |vLat| high.

Collisions: track boundaries — if car goes off asphalt, slow down (grass friction) and add particles; walls? For simple fun, grass slowdown + outer barrier? Keep it forgiving: grass slows, plus solid barriers around outer loop? Better no hard walls, just grass slowdown (off-track penalty) but world bounds collision. AI also slows on grass.

Car-car collisions: circle-based push apart with impulse — needed for racing fun.

AI: target point ahead on centerline (lookahead ~ 120-220 based on speed), steer toward it, throttle to target speed based on curvature ahead. Avoid other cars slightly. Rubberband lightly for fun.

Lap tracking: each car tracks nearest centerline sample index and progress; lap increments when crossing start index going forward after passing half track (to avoid cheating). Compute total progress = lap + i/N. Position ranking by total progress.

Race: 3 laps, 4 cars. Countdown. After finish, results panel with times, restart button.

Rendering:
- Background grass: tiled procedural texture generated to offscreen canvas (noise + subtle stripes), drawn with pattern. Draw world in camera transform, pattern works in world coords.
- Track: build path from centerline (inner edge/outer edge) using offset curves; fill asphalt with gradient-ish color? Draw wide stroke along centerline as asphalt (lineWidth = width) with rounded joins — easiest! Then kerbs: stroke with width width+18 in red/white alternating using dashes? Kerb can be done by stroking a path with lineDash [40,40] twice: red dashes offset. Approach: stroke centerline with width = W+22, color red; then stroke with dash pattern for white? Actually classic kerb alternating red/white on the edges only. Easier: draw outer stroke W+20 white, then dashed red stroke W+20 with dash [34,34] but it would fill full width not just edges. Hmm.

Approach: draw the track edges as two separate offset paths (left and right) stroked with alternating red/white segments. Compute offset polylines, then draw each segment with color depending on segment index (every ~4 segments toggles). That's easy: for each edge polyline, loop segments, alternate colors every 3 samples with thick lineWidth 10. Kerbs only on corners? Full loop is fine and looks racing-like.

- Asphalt texture: overlay subtle noise via pattern with low alpha; skid marks persistent layer canvas (world-sized offscreen, draw skid marks when drifting) — nice touch. World size 2400x1600 offscreen at maybe 0.5 scale = 1200x800 to save memory. Draw tire marks as dark translucent lines. Also add rubber racing line darkening at center? skip.

- Start/finish line: checkered band across track at start, drawn rotated.
- Decorations: trees/bushes/tire stacks around track off-track... Need placement avoiding track. Use noise/random with distance check to centerline > W/2+60. Draw as canvas shapes: bushes circles, tire stacks, grandstand? Could add simple crowd dots. Keep modest for performance; pre-render decorations to a static offscreen layer (grass+decor+trees), but shadows of cars dynamic.

Actually pre-render entire static world (grass, track, kerbs, lines, start line, decorations) into one big offscreen canvas at scale 1 (2400x1600 = 15MB, fine) then blit with camera transform each frame. Skid marks layer separate at scale 0.5 or full. That guarantees performance.

- Car rendering: rounded body with shadow, wheels that turn with steering, brake lights, underglow? Draw in car's local transform. Player car distinct color (cyan) with white stripe, AI varied.

- Particles: tire smoke puffs (world), dust when off track, sparks on collision.

- HUD (DOM overlay for crispness): top-left lap/time panel, top-right minimap canvas, bottom-left speedometer arc via canvas or CSS. Use DOM elements with CSS styling. Bottom center on mobile touch buttons.

- Minimap: small canvas drawn each frame with track path from precomputed scaled points and car dots.

- Countdown overlay big numbers.

- Sound: engine oscillator (sawtooth) + lowpass + noise for tyres. Start audio on first user gesture. Mute button.

Responsiveness: HUD scale via clamp, touch controls show on coarse pointers / small screens.

Start behavior: capture script auto-starts by clicking selectors? `startForCapture` clicks a selector if CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR or default maybe. It will click something. Our game starts on user input (Enter / tap). For screenshot, the capture script clicks ... let me check capture-start logic to see which selector and whether it clicks.

Capture will click a visible button labeled "Start" / "Play". I'll have a title screen with a "START RACE" button. That gets clicked, countdown begins; screenshot after 1s will show countdown "3" maybe. Better: capture takes screenshot 1 second after click. Countdown starts at 3 length e.g., 3s total → screenshot shows "2"/"3" and cars on grid. That's a decent screenshot but less exciting. I could make countdown fast (1.6s) so at 1s shows "1" or GO. Hmm.

Alternative: Have title button "START" and start countdown lasting 3 sec. Screenshot shows grid + countdown. That's fine and shows the game. But I want a screenshot showing gameplay for my own verification. I'll use playwright-cli manually to capture gameplay after driving.

Let's structure files:
- index.html
- style.css
- js/game.js maybe single file ~1500 lines. Split into modules? Simpler single game.js is fine but big. I'll do a few modules for clarity: src/track.js, src/car.js, src/render.js, src/game.js, src/audio.js, src/input.js. Since static no bundler, type="module" works (served over http). Keep it maintainable. But default capture loads fine.

I'd rather write well-organized modules. Let's do:

index.html — DOM skeleton (HUD, overlays, touch controls).
css/style.css
js/utils.js — math helpers
js/track.js — track geometry generation, path, minimap data, prerender track/world.
js/car.js — physics + rendering cars.
js/ai.js — opponent controller.
js/audio.js — WebAudio engine sounds.
js/main.js — game loop, race state, HUD, input, camera, particles, minimap, screenshots-friendly.

Let's think details carefully.

Coordinate system: world 2400x1500, track loop based on parametric center (1240, 760), rx=880, ry=520.

r(θ) = 1 + 0.13*sin(2θ+0.4) + 0.09*sin(3θ-0.8) + 0.05*cos(5θ)
point = center + (rx*r*cosθ, ry*r*sinθ)

Check extremes: rx*r max ~ 880*1.25=1100 → x 140..2340; ry 520*1.25=650 → y 110..1410. World 2480x1520 maybe. Let's set world W=2500, H=1550, center (1250,775), rx=860, ry=500, so margin ~ 860*1.27=1092 → x 158..2342 good; y 500*1.27=635 → 140..1410 good.

Sample N=480 points. Compute cumulative length. W=200 track width.

Start line at sample 0 (θ=0 → right side, heading +y-ish?). Tangent direction counterclockwise? Parametric θ increasing moves counterclockwise in standard math coords but y is down in canvas, so going θ increasing goes clockwise visually... Direction doesn't matter, consistent.

Grid positions: behind start line, i.e., at s = length - offset backwards; compute pos & tangent. Cars: player at back of grid? For fairness and interest, start player 4th (last) so there's overtaking. Good for gameplay. Grid: 2x2, offsets 45 & 105 behind line, lateral ±48.

Track width 200, car length 48, width 26.

Physics constants (world px, seconds):
maxSpeed ~ 720 px/s (feels fast with zoom 0.8 on 1280 → 576 px/s on screen).
accel 520 px/s², brake 900, reverse max 180, drag: vLong *= (1 - 0.55*dt) roughly; better linear: dragCoef 0.9.
Steering: maxSteer 0.55 rad wheel angle, wheelbase 46. yawRate = v * tan(steer)/wheelbase → at v=400, steer 0.3 → 400*0.309/46 = 2.7 rad/s way too high. Real units: wheelbase in world px 46 too small relative to speed. Use scaled: yawRate = v/ wheelbase * tan(steer) with effective wheelbase = 90? at 400 → 1.37 rad/s still fast. Hmm arcade: use yawRate = steerInput * turnRate * speedFactor where turnRate ~ 2.6 rad/s at moderate speed decaying at high speed. Simpler and controllable:

```
turn = maxTurn * (1 - 0.45*min(speed/maxSpeed,1)) * min(abs(vLong)/80, 1) * sign(vLong)
angle += steerInput * turn * dt
```
maxTurn ~ 3.0 rad/s. At full speed 720: turn=3*0.55=1.65 rad/s → turning radius v/ω = 436px. Track corners radius ~ 300-600. okay. Add handbrake yaw boost 1.35x.

Grip: lateral velocity damping: vLat *= exp(-grip*dt), grip = 6 (normal) → kills lateral quickly; handbrake grip=1.4 for drift; grass grip 1.2 + extra friction. Reconstruct velocity: vel = forward*vLong + right*vLat.

Engine: vLong += throttle*accel*dt when throttle; rolling resistance vLong *= exp(-0.6*dt); speed cap maxSpeed. Off-track: maxSpeed*0.55, extra drag.

Brake: reduce vLong toward 0 at 1100/s, reverse if held when stopped.

Skid detection: abs(vLat) > 55 and speed > 120, or handbrake with speed>150 → emit skid marks + smoke.

Surface sampling: find nearest centerline distance; asphalt if dist < W/2 - 6; kerb if < W/2 + 8 (slows slightly); grass otherwise. Efficient: nearest sample search from cached index ±40 with occasional global? Use index caching per car and search window 60 around last index; centerline 480 samples, loop distance per frame small. Fine.

Progress: nearest idx; track crossing: maintain continuous lap progress. Use "lap + idx/N" but handle wrap: if idx jumps from ~479 to ~0 forward → lap++. If backwards wrap, lap--. Also require passing half lap? Standard crossing detection: since idx adjacency around loop, wrap only happens near start. Compute delta index adjusted with wrap; accumulate `raceProgress += delta / N`. Then lap = floor(progress) + start offset? Cars start behind line at negative progress. Simpler: define progress = lapCount + idx/N, with crossing detection: if prevIdx > N*0.75 and idx < N*0.25 → lap++. If prevIdx < N*0.25 and idx > N*0.75 → lap-- (going backwards over line). For ranking multiply. Cars start behind line: their idx near end (N - offsets). So lap starts 0, they need to cross line to complete first crossing? That'd make laps count at start line crossing → 3 laps after crossing 3 times, consistent: lapDisplay = min(lapCount+1, 3). Start behind line, first crossing increments lap to 1 (meaning starting lap 1?) Hmm.

Cleaner: treat lap timer start when crossing start line first time? Simpler approach: total progress distance along path from start line; cars start at negative progress (behind line). When progress crosses N (one full lap from 0), lap completes. Track `dist` = continuous path distance (can be negative at start). On each frame, update progress using nearest index with unwrapping: `prog = continuous` in sample units. Initialize prog = idx - N for cars behind start (idx near N). Then lap = floor(prog / N) ... Cars start at prog=-30 samples; after crossing line prog passes 0; completed laps = floor(prog/N) plus? Actually if start at -30 samples and prog reaches +480-30? Let's simply count complete laps when prog >= N, 2N, 3N. Since start at -30, the first "lap" includes 30 extra samples = tiny, but we cross start line immediately. Not a big deal but lap time from race start rather than line crossing. Fine: treat lap 1 begins at race start (standing start from grid, timing from GO). Standard.

Lap time: capture lapStartTime when lap increments. On finish third lap, stop.

Ranking: compare prog (continuous) among cars; finished cars ranked by finish time.

AI: target point = centerline at index (idx + lookaheadSamples) with lateral offset along racing line (maybe small offset per car to avoid stacking, and avoid player?). Steering: compute angle difference between heading and vector to target, clamped to input. Throttle: desired speed based on curvature ahead: compute max curvature over next ~ 25 samples; targetSpeed = clamp(sqrt(gripAccel/curvature)...). Simple: targetSpeed = maxSpeed * (1 - 0.55*curvatureNormalized). Use curvature = angle change per distance.

Compute curvature at index: |Δtangent angle| / ds. For sampled loop, precompute per-sample curvature smoothed. targetSpeed = min(maxSpeed, sqrt(maxLatAccel / (curvature + eps))) where maxLatAccel ~ 1400 px/s²? Let's compute: corner radius 300 → v = sqrt(1400*300)=648. Track corners likely radius 250..900. Then AI slows approaching corners using lookahead of 20 samples distance.

AI throttle control: if speed < target*0.98 → throttle 1, brake if > target*1.08. Plus rubberband: if far behind player, slight speed boost 5%.

AI also avoid car ahead: if another car within 70px in front within 25° → steer offset lateral and brake slightly.

Need AI not spin off: use same physics but with grip assist? Use same physics; steering computed will mostly keep on track. Add "recovery": if off track or pointing wrong, throttle reduced, steer toward centerline.

Collisions car-car: circles radius 22. Push apart positionally, exchange velocity component along normal with restitution 0.4. Effects.

Track limits for player: no walls, grass slows heavily. World bounds clamp.

Rendering details:

Prerendered world canvas (scale 1): 
1. fill grass base color #2f6b3a with noise: generate noise pattern 128x128 with random green speckles + mowed stripes (diagonal bands). Use pattern fill.
2. Draw track: 
   - shadow/edge: stroke centerline closed path width W+26 color dark #1b2a1f with alpha (edge dirt).

3. Decorations: trees (dark green clusters with trunk shadow) placed at random positions with min distance from centerline (W/2+55) and not overlapping each other; tire stacks (black circles w/ red rim) near corners; gravel traps? Add sand traps outside corners maybe too complex. Add grandstand near start straight: simple rectangles with crowd dots. Might be off camera often; keep simple: bushes + trees + tire stacks + sponsor boards along straights.
4. Outside world edge: darker green vignette / barrier? Add trees ring at edges.

For car shadows and skid layer: skid canvas world-size at 0.5 scale, drawn with transform; with fade? Persistent marks; clear on restart. Draw with lineWidth 6*0.5, color rgba(20,20,20,0.5). Good.

Cars are drawn each frame with camera transform: shadow ellipse offset, body shape rounded rect with gradient, cockpit, spoiler, wheels (front wheels rotated by steer), headlights, brake lights (when braking). Player has a subtle white arrow or ring? Add name labels above AI? no.

Draw order: shadow, skid layer, cars sorted by y? Not needed. Particles above.

Camera: center = player.pos + velocity*0.12, zoom = lerp based on speed 1.0→0.86 (fit track). Camera shake tiny on collision. Clamp camera to world? The world mostly filled; clamp so we don't see beyond world: camera center clamped to viewport half extents. World 2500x1550 at zoom 0.9 with 1280x720 → visible 1422x800; world bigger so fine.

Actually with warm look, I'd like slight camera rotation? Skip; fixed.

- Top bar: lap counter "LAP 1/3", race position "4/4", timers (race time, best lap, last lap).
- Speedometer bottom-right: canvas 150x150 arc with needle + digital km/h. Or simpler DOM: big number + bar. A circular gauge drawn on canvas looks nice. I'll make a small canvas gauge (drawn each frame) with arc ticks, digital speed, gear indicator (D/R).

Let me also include pause (Esc/P) and restart (R) while racing. Results overlay with "RACE AGAIN" button, plus stats.

Lap detection function per car each frame:
```
findClosest
d = idx - prevIdx adjust to [-N/2, N/2]
prog += d  (in sample units)
if prog - lastLapProg >= N ... 
```
Better: track continuous `prog` starting negative at grid:
Initialize each car's prog = idx - N (with idx from start placement near end). For player start behind line maybe idx = N-10. Then each frame delta using wrap; prog += delta. Lap = floor((prog + startOffset?) / N)+1... Let's define lap counting based on crossing multiples of N since race start origin at path sample 0. Cars starting at prog=-10. Completed laps = floor(prog / N) where prog negative initially → -1! Use completedLaps = max(0, floor(prog/N))? At prog=-10 floor=-1 → 0 good. As they cross start (prog 0..) laps still 0 until prog>=N. lapDisplay = completedLaps+1. Finish when completedLaps==LAPS. But timing: first lap includes the 10-sample head start; negligible (10 samples ≈ 20px). Fine.

import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'

const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()

const out = '/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots'
mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true })

const browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 })
const errors = []
try {
  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1100, height: 700 } })
  page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
  page.on('pageerror', e => errors.push('pageerror: ' + e.message))
  page.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') errors.push('console: ' + m.text()) })
  page.on('requestfailed', r => errors.push('requestfailed: ' + r.url() + ' ' + r.failure()?.errorText))

  await page.goto('http://127.0.0.1:3002/', { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 })
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__apex && window.__apex.state.mode === 'title')
  await page.waitForTimeout(400)
  console.log('TITLE mode:', await page.evaluate(() => window.__apex.state.mode))
  await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, 'check-title.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 72 })

  await page.click('#startBtn')
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__apex.state.mode === 'countdown', { timeout: 3000 })
  console.log('COUNTDOWN mode:', await page.evaluate(() => window.__apex.state.mode))
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__apex.state.mode === 'racing', { timeout: 8000 })
  console.log('RACING mode reached')

  // Drive for a while: full throttle + slight steering corrections.
  await page.keyboard.down('KeyW')
  await page.waitForTimeout(1200)
  await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, 'check-race-early.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 72 })

  const samples = []
  for (let i = 0; i < 18; i++) {
    const s = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const a = window.__apex
      return {
        mode: a.state.mode,
        lap: a.state.playerLap,
        speed: Math.round(a.playerCar.kmh),
        x: Math.round(a.playerCar.x),
        y: Math.round(a.playerCar.y),
        raceTime: Math.round(a.state.raceTime * 10) / 10,
      }
    })
    samples.push(s)
    // steer toward track direction using simple bang-bang on angle error
    const steer = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const a = window.__apex
      const car = a.playerCar
      const target = a.track.points[car.trackIndex % a.track.N]
      const desired = Math.atan2(target.y - car.y, target.x - car.x)
      let d = desired - car.angle
      while (d > Math.PI) d -= Math.PI * 2
      while (d < -Math.PI) d += Math.PI * 2
      return d > 0.06 ? 'right' : d < -0.06 ? 'left' : 'none'
    })
    await page.keyboard.up('KeyA')
    await page.keyboard.up('KeyD')
    if (steer === 'left') await page.keyboard.down('KeyA')
    if (steer === 'right') await page.keyboard.down('KeyD')
    await page.waitForTimeout(400)
  }
  await page.keyboard.up('KeyW')
  await page.keyboard.up('KeyA')
  await page.keyboard.up('KeyD')
  console.log('SAMPLES', JSON.stringify(samples))

  await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, 'check-race-latest.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 72 })

  // Pause / resume
  await page.keyboard.press('KeyP')
  await page.waitForTimeout(250)
  const paused = await page.evaluate(() => window.__apex.state.mode)
  console.log('PAUSE mode:', paused)
  const pauseHidden = await page.locator('#pauseScreen').evaluate(el => el.classList.contains('hidden'))
  console.log('pause screen hidden while paused:', pauseHidden)
  await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, 'check-pause.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 72 })
  await page.keyboard.press('KeyP')
  await page.waitForTimeout(250)
  console.log('RESUME mode:', await page.evaluate(() => window.__apex.state.mode))

  // Exercise finish/results by forcing enough laps: drive fast-forward via state not easy; instead test restart.
  await page.keyboard.press('KeyR')
  await page.waitForTimeout(300)
  console.log('RESTART mode:', await page.evaluate(() => window.__apex.state.mode))

  // Mobile viewport with touch controls presence
  const mobile = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 }, isMobile: true, hasTouch: true })
  mobile.on('pageerror', e => errors.push('mobile pageerror: ' + e.message))
  mobile.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') errors.push('mobile console: ' + m.text()) })
  await mobile.goto('http://127.0.0.1:3002/', { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 })
  await mobile.waitForFunction(() => window.__apex && window.__apex.state.mode === 'title')
  await mobile.waitForTimeout(400)
  await mobile.screenshot({ path: join(out, 'check-mobile-title.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 72 })
  await mobile.click('#startBtn')
  await mobile.waitForFunction(() => window.__apex.state.mode === 'racing', { timeout: 9000 })
  await mobile.locator('[data-act="throttle"]').dispatchEvent('pointerdown')
  await mobile.waitForTimeout(1300)
  await mobile.locator('[data-act="throttle"]').dispatchEvent('pointerup')
  await mobile.screenshot({ path: join(out, 'check-mobile-race.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 72 })
  console.log('MOBILE mode:', await mobile.evaluate(() => window.__apex.state.mode))
  await mobile.close()

  console.log('ERRORS', errors.length ? JSON.stringify(errors) : 'none')
} finally {
  await browser.close()
}
